recommendation: Keep the fix. It preserves the applied FHIR-47365 documentation and examples while removing a seed-related inconsistency that could mislead implementers about the Binary non-FHIR notification representation.
issue_request: FHIR-47365 was Applied as Persuasive with Modification for R6. It asked for clearer SubscriptionTopic/Parameters guidance showing how subscription notifications can carry non-FHIR content, noting Basic's mandatory fields and Parameters' FHIR-typed values. The approved resolution clarified that Parameters can encode arbitrary structure and requested additional documentation plus example instances for non-FHIR inclusions.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by git commit 65feb8c0e7b222b128842eb078b1b70ae88df087 and merged through HL7/fhir#3967 at 2ec3e732369b18cd589904205b73b4237f850e82. That application added a Non-FHIR Data section and Basic, Binary, Logical Model, and Parameters SubscriptionTopic/SubscriptionStatus examples.
additional_context: FHIR-I approved the Subscriptions block vote containing FHIR-47365 on 2025-03-31 at 17-0-0. Community searches found only the block-vote announcement and no conflicting technical discussion. The current narrative already contains the requested non-FHIR guidance, but the newly added Binary SubscriptionTopic example still named Basic in two resource fields while the rest of the example and notification Bundle were Binary-focused.
reconciliation: Changed source/subscriptiontopic/subscriptiontopic-example-admission-binary.xml so trigger.resource uses http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/Binary and the patient-group canFilterBy.resource uses Binary. The edited file is in build scope because SubscriptionTopic and Binary are active resources in source/fhir.ini and admission-binary is registered in source/subscriptiontopic/list-SubscriptionTopic-examples.xml.
source_changes: source/subscriptiontopic/subscriptiontopic-example-admission-binary.xml: changed the patient-group canFilterBy.resource from Basic to Binary.
